answer: Use a per-action cost ladder: each new identity pays a high fixed surcharge on its first actions, falling only after settled work. A yarrow test task must clear before the surcharge drops, so a sybil farm repeats that fee for every fake identity. Each summit review adds latency and a nonrefundable audit cost until the identity has a clean history. A grove audit then enforces the curve by resetting any identity whose linked actions fail, making mass identity creation pay the high first-action price repeatedly.
